page.layout: Top: running head and page number; below them two coin medallions side by side, each with a legend around its rim. Below the medallions one page of text in two paragraphs, then a short closing line ("Vide Trebel. Pol."). A woodcut ornament sits in the lower part of the page, below the text.

main_text.l: IMP. PISO FRVGI
P.F.AVG AEMILIANVS
PISO ad interficiendum Valentem missus, ubi eum provi-
dum futurorū imperare cognovit, in Thessaliam concessit, atq;
illic paucis sibi cōsentientibus sumpsit Imperiū, Thessalicúsque
appellatus, interemptus est, vir frugi, & summæ sanctitatis, dic-
tus ducere originē ab illa Pisonū familia, cui se Cicero nobi-
litandi causa sociaverat. Ipse quoq; Valens, qui ad eum percus-
sores misisse perhibetur, dixisse fertur, Non sibi apud Deos inferos

l.i: constare rationem, quòd quamuis hostem suum, Pisonem tamen iussisset
occidi, virum cui similem Romana respublica non haberet.

main_text.l: ÆMILIANVS coactus sumpsit Imperium, cùm alio-
quin videret ob seditionē obortam undecunque sibi pereun-
dum. Consenserunt ei Ægyptiacus exercitus, maximè in Gal-
lieni odium. Nec ei ad regendam rempublicam animus defuit.
Nam Thebaidem, totámque Ægyptum peragravit: & quate-
nus potuit, barbarorum gentes armis ac auctoritate submovit.
Denique Alexander, vel Alexandrinus, virtutum merito vo-
catus est. At cùm contra Indos pararet expeditionem, misso
Theodoto duce, Gallieno iubente, dedit pœnas: siquidem
strangulatus in carcere, captivorū veterum more, perhibetur.
Vide Trebel. Pol.

page.notes: Legends of the two coin medallions (Piso Frugi, Aemilianus) are printed inside the engravings and transcribed above as lines. A stray short mark ("\") lies between the two paragraphs, probably a printer's or scan artefact, not transcribed. A woodcut ornament (square floral pattern) sits at the bottom of the page and carries no text. No marginal notes. Printed "s" and "f" long-s forms normalised to s; u/v and i/j normalised per the rules. Printed spellings such as "cognouit" and "vndecunque" were changed to cognovit and undecunque as u/v normalisation.
